claim: A Docker MCP Registry submission is a pull request adding servers/<name>/server.yaml; the licence must permit consumption, local servers need a Dockerfile in the source repo, source.commit pins a commit, CI must pass and a Docker-team review is required.
title: Contributing to the Docker MCP Registry

claim: Registry configuration is declarative: config.parameters as JSON-schema inputs, config.env with templating, config.secrets stored outside env-var config, and run.volumes, run.command, run.user and run.disableNetwork for container behaviour.
title: docker/mcp-registry docs/configuration.md

claim: The registry has two tiers: Docker-built images that Docker builds, signs and publishes with provenance and SBOMs, and community-built images that get container isolation only.
title: docker/mcp-registry README

claim: The MCP gateway supports stdio, SSE and streaming transports, with a port for HTTP listeners, a localhost auth token, a long-lived mode for stateful servers, and network blocking and signature verification flags.
title: docker mcp gateway run

claim: Each MCP Toolkit tool runs in its own container restricted to one CPU and two gigabytes of memory with no host filesystem access by default.
title: MCP Toolkit

claim: A container on Docker Desktop reaches a service on the host through the special DNS name host.docker.internal.
title: Explore networking how-tos

claim: GPU passthrough in Docker Desktop works only on Windows with the WSL2 backend.
title: GPU support in Docker Desktop for Windows

claim: MCP tool annotations are hints, not guarantees; destructiveHint and openWorldHint default to true, clients must treat annotations as untrusted unless the server is trusted, and servers must validate inputs, rate-limit invocations and sanitise outputs.
title: Model Context Protocol specification 2025-06-18, Tools

claim: The Left 4 Dead AI Director estimates each player's emotional intensity and drives a build-up, sustain, fade and relax loop, with boss encounters deliberately exempt from adaptive pacing.
title: The AI Systems of Left 4 Dead

claim: Every utterance is a query of world-state facts against a writer-authored rule database where the most specific matching rule wins, variation comes from groups of hand-written alternates, and repetition is suppressed by facts with expiry times.
title: AI-driven Dynamic Dialog through Fuzzy Pattern Matching

claim: Firewatch's interrupt-heavy bark system desynced internal state when interrupted threads did not finish, so the character could know things the player did not, which forced explicit uninterruptible brackets around critical conversations.
title: Do You Copy? Dialog System and Tools in Firewatch

claim: Kokoro-82M is an 82-million-parameter text-to-speech model released under Apache-2.0 including the weights.
title: Kokoro-82M model card

claim: Chatterbox is MIT-licensed, exposes exaggeration and cfg_weight controls, and every output carries a neural watermark.
title: resemble-ai/chatterbox README

claim: Piper's maintained line moved to GPL-3.0 while the archived original repository is MIT.
title: OHF-Voice/piper1-gpl README

claim: Orpheus-TTS code is Apache-2.0 but its weights are under the Llama 3.2 Community License, and it streams with roughly 200 ms time to first audio.
title: canopyai/Orpheus-TTS README

claim: F5-TTS code is MIT but its pre-trained models are CC-BY-NC because of the Emilia training data.
title: SWivid/F5-TTS README
